Fit the original MODGEE model

Source: R/fit_modgee.R
fit_modgee.Rd

Estimate detection parameters, cumulative extinction and dark extinctions from species detection histories. This implementation supports mutually exclusive species groups sharing a temporal extinction baseline.

Usage

fit_modgee(
  M,
  groups = NULL,
  reference_group = NULL,
  do_k = FALSE,
  bootstrap = NULL,
  CI = 0.95
)

Arguments

M

A numeric or logical matrix with species in rows and equally spaced time intervals in columns. Entries must be 0 or 1, with no missing values. A value of 1 indicates at least one detection during an interval; 0 indicates no recorded detection, not confirmed absence or extinction. Row names are required and must identify species. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed before checking that names are nonempty and unique. Column names are required and must convert to finite, unique, strictly increasing, equally spaced numeric time labels. They are the only source of time labels; there is no separate times argument. Character and complex matrices are not accepted. Logical entries are converted to numeric 0/1 values.

groups

Optional CSV path, two-column data frame (species, group), character vector, factor, or numeric/logical 0/1 membership matrix. Names are trimmed and matched to all input species, including all-zero rows. Unnamed vectors and matrices follow input row order. Extra named species are ignored with a warning. Each species must have one group. CSV and character labels use radix sorting; factors use level order; membership matrices use column order. The first active group is the reference unless reference_group is specified. Empty groups are removed and reported. Every active group needs at least two repeated-detection species (a minimum safeguard, not a guarantee of statistical identifiability).

reference_group

Optional single group name. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed. When NULL, the first active group under the default ordering is the reference. An explicit name overrides factor levels and membership-matrix column order; other groups retain their relative order. The named group must contain recorded species and meet the repeated-detection requirement. Supplying a reference without groups is an error. The reference log multiplier is fixed at zero, so its hazard multiplier is one. The selected name is returned in groups$reference_group.

do_k

Logical scalar. If TRUE, compare the fixed-k model with a model that estimates a single k shared by all species. The two models share the first-stage detection estimates and use the same conditional likelihood in the extinction stage. For the alternative, the extinction hazard is m[t] * d[i]^k * l[group[i]], with the group multiplier equal to 1 when groups are absent. The alternative starts at k = 0. Main estimates use k = 0.

bootstrap

NULL (default), or a positive integer giving the number of scheduled full-pipeline species bootstrap replicates. Failed and nonconverged replicates count toward this number and are not resampled.

CI

Confidence level strictly between 0 and 1; default 0.95. Intervals are pointwise percentile intervals (quantile type 7).

Value

A list containing the following components:

summary

A named list with the following entries, in order:

baseline_timestep, final_timestep

First and last numeric column labels of the supplied matrix (calendar years when year labels are supplied).

excluded_species

Number of all-zero rows in the supplied matrix.

known_species

Number of nonzero rows.

singleton_species

Number of species detected in exactly one timestep.

known_extant

Expected surviving recorded species: known_species - known_extinct. This is not the number detected in the final timestep.

known_extinct

Sum of extinction probabilities over recorded species.

dark_extinct

Estimated unrecorded extinctions; negative estimates are retained. This is not the number of all-zero rows.

total_extinct

known_extinct + dark_extinct.

original_richness

known_species + dark_extinct.

cumulative_extinction_rate

Final cumulative extinction proportion, on the 0–1 scale; equals total_extinct / original_richness.

AIC

Fixed-k main-model AIC, using the second-stage conditional log likelihood and the original two-stage parameter-count convention: 2 * p - 2 * logLik, where p = (R - 1) + T + (T - 3) + (G - 1); logLik is the internal second-stage conditional log likelihood; R is the number of repeated-detection species, T the number of timesteps, and G the number of active groups (one without groups). Returns NA if either main fitting stage did not converge. When do_k = TRUE, matches the fixed-k comparison row.

parameters

Named vectors d, h and m. Grouped models also have l, the actual hazard multipliers, with reference value one. The starting values starts$ls_start remain log multipliers.

curve

Data frame: time, h, m, cumulative_extinction_rate. With groups, m is the reference hazard, and the overall rate is weighted by inferred baseline richness.

species

Data frame in original input order, with columns: species, belonged_group (only with groups), detected_timesteps, is_singleton, first_detection_timestep, last_detection_timestep, d, p_extinct, estimated_extinction_year. Detection timesteps are counted, not listed. First and last detections use actual numeric column labels. Estimated extinction year is the conditional mean extinction timestep mapped onto those labels, not a confirmed extinction date. All-zero rows have zero detected timesteps, FALSE for is_singleton, and NA for detection years and estimates. Undefined extinction times are NA.

groups

NULL without groups; otherwise matching information, species_group, membership matrix H, active levels, reference_group, removed_groups, and matching.

group_results

NULL without groups; otherwise a list of two data frames:

curve

group, time, m, cumulative_extinction_rate, for active groups only. The hazard m is the group's own hazard.

summary

group, then l (the actual hazard multiplier, not its logarithm), followed by the same columns as the overall summary, except AIC. Counts and estimates refer to each group. Supplied groups containing only all-zero species are included for counting; their dark_extinct, total_extinct, original_richness and cumulative_extinction_rate are NA because these groups are not fitted. The reference group has l = 1; groups excluded from fitting have l = NA. Group multipliers match those in parameters$l.

do_k

NULL unless requested; otherwise the existing fixed-k versus free-k comparison table. Main outputs always use the fixed-k model.

status, converged, convergence

Completion flags, optimizer diagnostics and convergence information.

bootstrap

NULL unless requested; bootstrap settings, status, interval tables, diagnostics and compact replicate estimates.

M, times

Validated input matrix and numeric time labels.

starts

Starting values, with species entries in input order.

Details

Active groups have at least one recorded species in the supplied analysis matrix. Groups with only all-zero rows, or unused factor levels, are removed from fitting. Each active group must additionally have at least two species detected in two or more timesteps; otherwise fitting stops.

Prepare the analysis matrix before calling this function. In particular, aggregate annual records if necessary and select the analysis baseline using read_matrix() or other preparation code. This function does not aggregate, subset, relabel or reorder time columns. It does not generate missing species names or time labels.

Use numeric column names such as "1870" and "1880", not "1870s" or "X1870". To use interval indices, explicitly assign column names such as "1", "2", and so on. Invalid or duplicate time labels are reported with their original column positions and names. Adjacent spacings must differ from the first spacing by no more than an absolute tolerance of 1e-8, as in read_matrix(). The optional preparation attribute is not required for fitting and is not used instead of validating the matrix itself.

The current implementation supports 4 to 215 time intervals and requires at least two species detected in at least two intervals each. These are minimum computational requirements, not guarantees that the data contain enough information for reliable estimation.

All-zero species are retained in the species table but excluded from fitting. Their parameter and extinction estimates are NA. Species detected in exactly one interval are treated as singletons using the original procedure.

The reference species is moved to the first row internally. The public species table and parameters$d retain the original input order. Internal reordering does not change public row order.

Use set.seed() before fitting to reproduce the random starting values. Optimization can still depend on starting values and the numerical environment. A normal convergence code does not establish a global optimum or validate the ecological assumptions.

Interpreting the estimates

The parameter m is not an extinction proportion. The corresponding interval extinction probability is 1 - exp(-m); cumulative extinction is 1 - exp(-cumsum(m)). The first, second and final interval extinction parameters are fixed at zero by the original implementation, not independently estimated as zero. With groups, replace m by m * l for each group. Overall cumulative extinction is not calculated from the reference m alone and is not an unweighted average of group curves.

p_extinct is a species-level probability of extinction by the final interval, conditional on its detection history and the fitted parameters.

Expected extinction times and their variances are conditional on extinction. The variance is in squared interval units. estimated_extinction_year maps interval indices onto the supplied time labels; it is not an exact date of extinction. Conditional times may be undefined (NaN) when the fitted probability of extinction is zero.

Dark extinctions represent losses without a recorded detection in the analysis period. The estimate is not a count of supplied all-zero rows. A negative estimate is not a literal negative number of species; it indicates that the estimate needs interpretation in light of the data and model assumptions.

Bootstrap and recovery

Nonzero species rows are sampled globally with replacement. Every replicate refits detection, extinction, group and singleton parameters at fixed k = 0. The reference group and active group set remain fixed; invalid samples are saved as failures. All-zero rows are not sampled. Negative dark extinction estimates are retained. No species-level or parameter intervals are computed.

Checkpoints are written below getwd()/modgee_bootstrap after the original fit and after every replicate. Sampling plans and fitting random states are saved before fitting. Rerun the same call in the same working directory to resume. An interrupted replicate restarts from its saved sample and initial random state; optimizer iterations within a replicate are not checkpointed. Completed failures and nonconverged fits are not retried. Increase bootstrap to extend a task, or change CI to recompute intervals without refitting. A smaller request summarizes only the first requested replicates.

An existing task owns its saved seed; set.seed does not reset that task. Use a different persistent working directory for an independent run. Changing the input, model implementation or numerical dependency versions starts a new task. Tasks are protected by a process lock. Invalid sampling plans stop recovery; corrupt result files are quarantined and the saved sample is fitted again. Write failures stop execution.

Bootstrap restores the caller's random state. Reproducibility assumes the same numerical environment. Only fully converged replicates with finite values for the requested metric enter its interval. Fewer than two values yield NA endpoints; fewer than 100 successful replicates produce a warning. Ten replicates are suitable only for demonstrations.

The bootstrap component contains settings, status, summary, curve, group_results, diagnostics and replicates. Summary tables use metric, estimate, lower, upper and n_valid; curve tables replace metric with time. Group tables also contain group. estimate is always the original point estimate. Six summary metrics receive intervals: known_extant, known_extinct, dark_extinct, total_extinct, original_richness and cumulative_extinction_rate. The compact replicate tables have a replicate index and a value column. Diagnostics retain warnings, errors and convergence codes for each attempt. The original do_k comparison is cached separately and is never repeated for bootstrap samples.

Usage Examples


# Run or resume a bootstrap task in the current working directory.
result_bootstrap <- fit_modgee(
  M = example_M, groups = example_groups,
  reference_group = "primary + old secondary", bootstrap = 10
)
result_bootstrap$bootstrap$status
result_bootstrap$bootstrap$curve

# Fit without groups using automatic starting values.
set.seed(123)
result <- fit_modgee(M = example_M)
result$summary

# Fit groups using the default reference group.
set.seed(123)
result_grouped <- fit_modgee(
  M = example_M,
  groups = example_groups
)
result_grouped$groups$reference_group
result_grouped$group_results$summary

# Select the reference group explicitly.
set.seed(123)
result_reference <- fit_modgee(
  M = example_M,
  groups = example_groups,
  reference_group = "primary + old secondary"
)

# Compare fixed-k and free-k models for grouped data.
set.seed(123)
result_grouped_k <- fit_modgee(
  M = example_M,
  groups = example_groups,
  reference_group = "primary + old secondary",
  do_k = TRUE
)
result_grouped_k$do_k

# The k comparison is also available without groups.
set.seed(123)
result_k <- fit_modgee(M = example_M, do_k = TRUE)
result_k$do_k

# Supply named group labels instead of a two-column data frame.
group_labels <- setNames(example_groups[[2]], example_groups[[1]])
set.seed(123)
result_labels <- fit_modgee(M = example_M, groups = group_labels)
